solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Moving against him, the writer succeeded in competition honouring Poseidon (8,5)

indicatorNotes.Moving: letters that are moving do not stay where they were put, so AGAINST HIM is rearranged

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as ME
s. = succeeded, as in family trees

annotation.surface: An athlete wins a contest held for the sea god, beating a rival.
annotation.walkthrough: Only AGAINST HIM is mixed; ME and S are added whole at the end. 'Moving against him' reads as a wrestler's tactic, and 'succeeded in competition' as winning.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Isthmian Games were the ancient Greek festival held at Corinth in Poseidon's honour.

entries.clue: Headless maggot snaffled by young canary (9)

indicatorNotes.Headless: a word with no head has lost its first letter, so WORM becomes ORM
indicatorNotes.snaffled by: to snaffle is to grab and keep, so the young one holds the maggot inside itself

blocks.note: an infant is a young child; it wraps round the next piece
a maggot is a WORM; headless, (W)ORM

annotation.surface: A young songbird gobbles up a grub it has half-eaten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canary' sits at the end looking like a bird to match the maggot, but in slang a canary is someone who sings to the police.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a canary 'sings', telling the police what they know, which is what an informant does.

entries.clue: Catching rook, Pooh’s feline friend makes start (7)

indicatorNotes.Catching: what catches something holds it, so the friend's name closes round the rook

blocks.note: Tigger, the tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh; wraps round the R

annotation.surface: Tigger pounces on a bird, which gives it a start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Makes start' reads as 'gives a fright', but 'start' is a verb, set going, and 'makes' only links it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: setting off an event, as a gun's trigger sets off a shot.

entries.clue: With which condition one doesn’t normally feel great? (11)

annotation.definition: With which condition one doesn’t normally feel great?

blocks.note: the surface wants an illness that leaves you under the weather
read literally: a condition in which you feel great, mighty, as normal people don't

annotation.surface: A question about an illness that stops you feeling well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feel great' reads as 'feel healthy'; take it literally: this is the condition of feeling great, that is grand and all-powerful, which normal people do not.
annotation.definitionFit: Megalomania is the delusion of one's own greatness, so its sufferer abnormally feels great in the grand sense.

entries.clue: Author having four sisters in family occupying rural cottage (6)

annotation.definition: Author having four sisters in family

indicatorNotes.occupying: the answer occupies, lives inside, the words that follow

annotation.surface: A writer from a big family living in a country cottage.
annotation.walkthrough: The four sisters are the March girls of Little Women; the author herself was one of four sisters too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women, about the four March sisters.

entries.clue: Lovely keyboard instrument in county once (9)

annotation.surface: A beautiful organ found somewhere in the countryside long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a county of south Wales, split up in 1974, hence 'once'.
annotation.definitionFit: A former county: Glamorgan was abolished as a single county in the 1974 reorganisation.

entries.clue: Bloom reserving different name for female who knows best (6,6)

indicatorNotes.reserving: to reserve something is to keep it in hand, so the bloom holds the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: to bloom is to mature, come into full flower; it wraps round what follows

annotation.surface: A flower kept back under a different label for a know-all woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloom' is a verb here, not a flower. The definition leans on the saying 'Mother Nature knows best'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: nature personified as a wise woman, and proverbially she knows best.

entries.clue: Grass skirts with jumper in an estuary (10)

indicatorNotes.skirts: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the grass goes round WITH

blocks.note: to grass is to inform on someone, so a grass is one who shops people; it wraps round AND

annotation.surface: A grass skirt worn with a sweater at the seaside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' and 'jumper' paint a wardrobe. In British slang a grass is an informer, and the jumper is a small leaping crustacean.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by habit: these tiny crustaceans leap about on sandy shores and estuary mud.

entries.clue: Negotiator in attempt to gamble? Small point (2-7)

blocks.note: have a go = make an attempt

annotation.surface: A deal-maker taking a small punt.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and full stop split the clue into two scraps, but it is one long chain of pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a go-between carries terms back and forth between two parties, as a negotiator does.

entries.clue: Good hill climbing finds poet’s cave (4)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down entry, climbing means going upwards, so the hill is read from the bottom

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

annotation.surface: A walker going up a fine hill comes across a cave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' warns that the answer is a literary word, a short form of grotto.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary word: poets shorten grotto to grot, hence 'poet's'.

entries.clue: Attend a match on sparsely settled land, or prevaricate? (4,5,3,4)

blocks.note: to attend is to BE AT
a boxing bout is a match
the bush is the Australian outback

annotation.surface: Going to a game out in the wilds, or dodging the question.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is split into new words: BE AT A BOUT, (on) THE BUSH.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to beat about the bush is to avoid coming to the point.

entries.clue: Follower crossing Republican’s path (5)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to go across it, here spanning it so the letter sits inside

blocks.note: a tail is someone following you; it wraps round R

annotation.surface: A supporter getting in a Republican politician's way.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rough track through country is both.

entries.clue: Nobleman with award for organ piece? (7)

blocks.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour

annotation.surface: An aristocrat receives a prize for an organ composition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ piece' suggests music; the organ is the ear and the piece a part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: the ear is an organ of the body and the lobe is a piece of it.

entries.clue: Cold war aftermath? Tough to secure outright victory on retreating! (7,6)

indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the tough holds the victory inside
indicatorNotes.retreating: what retreats goes backwards, so ON's letters are reversed

blocks.note: a nut, as in 'hard nut', is a tough guy; wraps round the victory
a clear win is an outright one

annotation.surface: A call to win the Cold War outright without giving ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold war' looks like the US-Soviet stand-off; the question mark flags a pun, since after a nuclear war the world would literally turn cold.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on 'cold war': the predicted global chill after nuclear war is a literally cold aftermath of war.

entries.clue: Cast of Brief Encounter (5)

blocks.note: not the film but a short affair

annotation.surface: The actors in the 1945 film Brief Encounter.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make you think of the film and its cast; lower-case, a brief encounter is a short affair, a FLING, and to fling is to cast.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to throw something, and a short-lived romance.

entries.clue: Talk to an eccentric old goat periodically in city (11)

annotation.surface: Chatting to a batty old goat now and then somewhere in town.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'eccentric old goat' looks like one character, but 'eccentric' is working on the words either side of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chattanooga is a city in Tennessee.

entries.clue: Goldfinger having sport among spooks from the East (5)

indicatorNotes.among: something among others sits in their midst, so the sport goes inside the spooks
indicatorNotes.from the East: in an across entry the east is the right-hand end, so read from there, right to left

blocks.note: spooks are spies; the CIA is the US spy agency; it wraps round RU

annotation.surface: The Bond villain playing a game among Eastern spies.
annotation.walkthrough: CI(RU)A is built first, then the whole thing is read backwards. Goldfinger's first name in the Bond novel means 'of gold'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by name: Auric is the Bond villain Goldfinger's first name, and the word itself means golden.

entries.clue: Fit pair to be worn by Latvian hunchback (9)

in cricket a pair is two ducks, two noughts in one match; they go round LETT

annotation.surface: Fitting a Latvian with a pair of something to wear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pair' is cricket slang: out for nought in both innings, two O's. The hunchback is the jester of Verdi's opera.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Verdi's Rigoletto is a hunchbacked court jester.

entries.clue: Nymph consorting with Zeus evoked memory (4)

blocks.note: the mountain nymph who kept Hera chattering while Zeus had his affairs
a trace of the past called back to mind

annotation.surface: A nymph with Zeus brings back memories.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence with 'evoked' as its verb; it is two separate definitions side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the nymph of Greek myth, and a noun for a reminder that recalls something earlier.

entries.clue: Name that is embracing artistic work? (8)

annotation.definition: Name that is embracing artistic work?

blocks.note: i.e. = that is; wraps round OP

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the name of a Muse, one who embraces artistic work.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: Calliope, Muse of epic poetry, is a name standing for artistic inspiration.

entries.clue: Medic with a touring car in Caribbean island (8)

blocks.note: A added after DOC; DOCA then wraps round MINI

annotation.walkthrough: 'A touring car' looks like one thing, a kind of car; it is 'a' going round the car.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dominica is an island nation in the eastern Caribbean.

entries.clue: Built with steeply angled sides, A&E accommodates female sheep (1-5)

blocks.note: A and E, with the next two pieces between them

entries.clue: Troublemaker co-partner at Vogue sacked (5,11)

blocks.note: a pastor is a minister of religion; minus P

annotation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests government; here it is a clergyman.

entries.clue: Enigmatic librarian! Run to me! Hippasus’ discovery revealed? (10,6)

indicatorNotes.Enigmatic: an enigma is a puzzle, so these letters are puzzled into a new order

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by history: Hippasus is credited with proving that some numbers cannot be written as fractions.

entries.clue: Game’s instruction given to those who’d dump illegally? (3-3-3)

annotation.definition2: instruction given to those who’d dump illegally?

blocks.note: an informal form of cricket where the batter must run after every hit

blocks.clueFragment: instruction given to those who’d dump illegally?
blocks.note: dump your rubbish, then make off

annotation.surface: Advice for fly-tippers, framed as the rules of a game.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain to tip is to dump rubbish, and illegal dumping is fly-tipping. Tip-and-run cricket makes the batter run whenever the ball is hit.

annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a panacea is a cure-all, supposed to make anyone well.

entries.clue: Semite near Moroccan location brought round by hospital in city (5,7)

annotation.surface: A shop sign repainted in lilac looks dazzling.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'brilliant' a paint colour; it is the definition, meaning sparkling or witty.

entries.clue: Secured loan without interest outside bank (8)

entries.clue: One such as Caiaphas: when drunk he is right to keep quiet (4,6)

entries.clue: Shopper in Cardiff perhaps eating fresh brie for snack (5,7)

BRIE rearranged, eaten by the rat

annotation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' looks like someone at the shops; it is someone who shops others, a rat.

entries.clue: On the drink heading to North Country (5)

annotation.surface: Someone drinking while travelling north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the drink' sounds like being drunk; it is two pieces, turned upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Niger is a country in West Africa.

entries.clue: Carriage reserved for small charge? (12)

blocks.note: the surface wants a booked railway carriage
not a cheap fare: the charge is a baby in someone's care

annotation.surface: A train carriage booked at a low fare.

entries.clue: Be in right gear, good enough to enter lot — centre includes parking (4,3,4)

annotation.surface: An expert on the loch, fishing with rod and line in a Highland glen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish with line' reads as angling; the line is a railway line.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Glen Garry is a Highland glen, and glen is the Scots word for a valley.

entries.clue: Conservationists in state bound to be heard (8,5)

indicatorNotes.to be heard: what is heard is spoken, so the word is spelt by its sound

blocks.note: state, as in state pension, means national

annotation.surface: Conservationists who are duty-bound in office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as obliged, but here it means tied up. The National Trust is a British heritage charity.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the charity preserves Britain's historic houses and countryside.
